finding.claim: SQL injection in ORDER BY: the unvalidated $_GET['sort'] value is concatenated directly into the query. An attacker can use sort expressions such as CASE/subselects for boolean or blind extraction of any data readable from the SQLite database (e.g. other tables), and can inject stacked expressions. list_users_safe() shows the allow-list fix that was not applied here.
finding.sink: $pdo->query("SELECT id, name FROM users ORDER BY " . $sort)

trace.note: string concatenated into SQL and executed via PDO::query

finding.guards_checked: No allow-list, no escaping, no parameter binding (ORDER BY cannot be bound anyway). No auth check in file. Contrast: list_users_safe (line 10-11) uses an allow-list map and is not vulnerable; find_user (line 16-17) uses a prepared statement and is not vulnerable.

verdict.reason: list.php:5-6 passes $_GET['sort'] unvalidated into the ORDER BY of a PDO::query with no allow-list, escaping or auth check (the allow-list at list.php:10-11 is only in list_users_safe); the function has no caller in this directory, but it is a web-facing file whose function takes $_GET directly, so it is reachable by any anonymous user once invoked.

verdict_facts.reason: list.php:5-6 concatenates $_GET['sort'] straight into the ORDER BY clause of a PDO::query call with no allow-list, escaping or auth check, whereas list_users_safe (list.php:10-11) has the allow-list that is missing here.
